name: Diwali
description: The festival of lights marking Rama's return to Ayodhya and the victory of light over darkness. Homes are lit with diyas, families exchange sweets, and fireworks light city skies.
traditions: Rangoli, Lakshmi puja, new account books in business communities, and sharing of mithai.

name: Holi
description: Spring festival of colours that began as a commemoration of Holika and Prahlada and of Krishna's play in Braj.
traditions: Holika dahan on the eve, gulal and water the next day, thandai and gujiya.

name: Navratri
description: Nine nights of devotion to the goddess in her many forms, culminating in Dussehra.
traditions: Garba and dandiya in Gujarat, golu displays in the south, fasting and kanya puja in the north.

name: Dussehra
description: Vijayadashami — Rama's victory over Ravana, and in Bengal the immersion of Durga.
traditions: Ramlila plays and burning of Ravana effigies; Ayudha puja in the south.

name: Ganesh Chaturthi
description: Birth festival of Ganesha, taken to the streets most famously in Maharashtra.
traditions: Public pandals, modak offerings, and visarjan immersions to the chant of Ganpati Bappa Morya.

name: Janmashtami
description: Midnight celebration of Krishna's birth, especially intense in Mathura–Vrindavan.
traditions: Dahi handi in Maharashtra, raslila, fasting until the birth hour.

name: Eid-ul-Fitr
description: Feast that ends Ramadan. The Islamic calendar shifts the Gregorian month each year; April is a representative marker.
traditions: Eid prayer, sheer khurma, new clothes, and charity (zakat al-fitr).

name: Eid-ul-Adha
description: Festival of sacrifice commemorating Ibrahim's devotion. Month varies with the lunar calendar.
traditions: Congregational prayer and sharing of qurbani meat with family and those in need.

name: Christmas
description: Nativity of Christ, celebrated with particular public warmth in Goa, Kerala, the Northeast, and Indian cities.
traditions: Midnight mass, cribs, cakes, and in Goa the feast of families after mass.

name: Makar Sankranti
description: Solar harvest festival as the sun enters Capricorn — Pongal, Magh Bihu, Lohri's neighbour, and kite-flying Uttarayan.
traditions: Sesame-jaggery sweets, ritual baths, and regional harvest feasts.

name: Pongal
description: Tamil harvest thanksgiving when fresh rice is boiled until it overflows — pongalo pongal.
traditions: Kolam, sugarcane, jallikattu in some districts, and honouring cattle on Mattu Pongal.

name: Onam
description: Kerala's harvest homecoming of the legendary king Mahabali.
traditions: Pookalam flower carpets, the Onam sadya feast, snake-boat races, and Kathakali.

name: Ugadi
description: Telugu and Kannada new year, named for the yuga's beginning.
traditions: Bevu-bella or ugadi pachadi mixing six tastes of the coming year.

name: Yugadi
description: Kannada new year aligned with the lunisolar calendar.
traditions: Mango-neem pachadi, new clothes, and panchanga shravana.

name: Gudi Padwa
description: Marathi new year marked by a gudi — a silk-topped banner — outside the home.
traditions: Puran poli, shrikhand, and processions in many towns.

name: Vishu
description: Malayalam new year whose first sight is the auspicious vishukkani arrangement.
traditions: Kanikkonna flowers, kane coins for children, and a sadya.

name: Rongali Bihu
description: Assamese spring new year and the most exuberant of the three Bihus.
traditions: Bihu dance, pepa horn, pitha sweets, and community husori singing.

name: Durga Puja
description: Bengal's greatest public festival: the goddess arrives, is adored, and returns to the river.
traditions: Artful pandals, dhak drums, sindoor khela, and Dashami immersions.

name: Kali Puja
description: Night of Kali coinciding with Diwali in Bengal, with lamps and tantric-folk worship.

name: Rath Yatra
description: Jagannath, Balabhadra, and Subhadra ride enormous chariots from Puri's temple to Gundicha.
traditions: Pulling the raths, chhera pahanra by the Gajapati king, and bahuda return.

name: Chhath Puja
description: Dawn and dusk offerings to Surya and Chhathi Maiya on river ghats of Bihar, east UP, and Jharkhand.
traditions: 36-hour fasts, thekua prasad, and standing in water at arghya.

name: Teej
description: Monsoon festival of Parvati, celebrated with swings, mehndi, and processions in Jaipur.
traditions: Ghevar, green bangles, and the Teej idol procession.

name: Jaisalmer Desert Festival
description: Cultural fair of the Thar with folk music, turban tying, and camel pageantry near the golden fort.

name: Pushkar Camel Fair
description: Livestock fair and Kartik pilgrimage around Pushkar lake, one of Rajasthan's great gatherings.

name: Hornbill Festival
description: Naga heritage festival at Kisama, nicknamed the Festival of Festivals.
traditions: Tribe-wise dances, morung displays, indigenous games, and night concerts.

name: Losar
description: Tibetan-Buddhist new year in Ladakh and Himalayan monasteries.
traditions: Guthuk soup, monastery masked dances, and offerings at household shrines.

name: Hemis Festival
description: Masked cham dances at Hemis Monastery honouring Padmasambhava.

name: Thrissur Pooram
description: Kerala's grandest temple pooram: competing elephant processions, ilanjithara melam, and fireworks.

name: Theyyam season
description: North Malabar ritual theatre in which dancers become living deities — a season more than a single day.

name: Kumbh Mela
description: The world's largest cyclical pilgrimage, rotating among Prayagraj, Haridwar, Nashik, and Ujjain.
traditions: Shahi snan of akharas at the sangam, camps of sadhus, and kalpavas.

name: Gangaur
description: Gauri festival of marital blessing, with ivory-and-terracotta processions in Jaipur and Udaipur.

name: Baisakhi
description: Harvest new year and the 1699 founding of the Khalsa by Guru Gobind Singh.
traditions: Nagar kirtan, bhangra, and visits to gurdwaras.

name: Guru Nanak Jayanti
description: Birth anniversary of Guru Nanak, the most widely kept Sikh gurpurab.
traditions: Akhand path, nagar kirtan, and langar at gurdwaras including Harmandir Sahib.

name: Maha Shivaratri
description: Great night of Shiva — vigils, abhisheka, and pilgrimages to Jyotirlinga shrines.
traditions: Night-long fasting, bael leaves, and processions at Varanasi, Ujjain, and Kedarnath's season.

name: Raksha Bandhan
description: Siblings tie the rakhi thread of protection and exchange sweets.
traditions: Rakhi, gifts, and in Rajasthan often ghevar.

name: Karva Chauth
description: North Indian fast kept from dawn until the moon is sighted, for a spouse's well-being.

name: Goa Carnival
description: Pre-Lenten parade introduced under the Portuguese, now a state-wide street festival.
traditions: King Momo, floats, and Konkani-Portuguese music.

name: Khajuraho Dance Festival
description: Classical dance against the Chandela temples, usually in late February.
